clusters.state_of_play: Canada has formally enacted dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion ($19.94 billion) of US goods, including steel, dairy, aluminum, fish, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, effective Sept 8, alongside a C$7.5 billion aid package for affected businesses and workers, as the US-Canada trade war continues to escalate following Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods and autos, his Lake Ontario rename threat, and personal attacks on Doug Ford. British Columbia Premier David Eby says the US can no longer be trusted and the relationship is permanently altered, while Doug Ford compares US treatment of Canada to China and insists Canada only wants a fair deal. Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc says a deal remains in both nations' interest, and US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins defends the trade war despite acknowledging farmer concerns, as some Republicans like Rep. Tom Barrett voice cautious hope for resolution. Trump has denied targeting one of Canada's official languages and separately called Canada the 'most difficult' nation the US deals with, while the White House drew ridicule after posting a botched AI-generated map relabeling the Great Lakes 'Lake America' and the Gulf of Mexico 'Gulf of America'.
